newsitem.title: USA: US minority-owned cos say hurt by 'old boy' network.
newsitem.headline: US minority-owned cos say hurt by 'old boy' network.

text.p: A survey of minority-owned businesses released Monday found that many came up against an "old-boy" network among corporate purchasers that limited minority opportunities to win a shrinking number of contracts.

The Chicago-area survey of 128 minority-owned firms and seven large corporations, conducted by the Chicago Urban League, showed purchasers for the corporations were narrowing the number of suppliers they wanted to deal with to control inventory and product quality.
About 85 percent of the minority business owners said the narrowing of suppliers had hurt their sales, and made access to contract opportunities more difficult.
Many said purchasers wanted longer track records than they could offer, and about three-quarters of the minority-owned firms reported they had cash-flow problems.
Moreover, 74 percent of minority vendors said that a corporate "old boy" network continued to operate in purchasing, often bypassing affirmative action programs in the public and private sectors.
"Minority-owned businesses need to have direct contact with key personnel in corporations' purchasing processes to succeed," Urban League President James Compton said.

"The relative absence of minority-owned firms in manufacturing and wholesaling means that African Americans stand outside of the largest and most important sector of the U.S. and local economy -- business-to-business transactions," Compton said in a statement accompanying the survey.
The non-profit organization said previous national surveys showed large corporations placed between 2 percent and 5 percent of their purchases with minority-owned firms.
